subject: Mgmt + Data Fabric: private VPC attachment and reference diagram review
messages:

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22 14:03 PST
Subject: Mgmt + Data Fabric: private VPC attachment and reference diagram review

Hi team —

Attaching the first-pass reference diagram for the private VPC we're provisioning for StellarAnalytics (mgmt-data-fabric-v1.png) and a short runbook draft for tenant segmentation. Goal for this thread: 1) validate the control-plane placement and HA options, 2) confirm acceptable egress/NAT model for tenant workloads, and 3) agree on handoff artifacts (what Rackline needs to provision ahead of cutover).

High-level notes in the doc:
- Management fabric is a dedicated /26 per colo; control-plane (k8s control plane + rendezvous proxies) will be in the management fabric with eBGP peering to the customer edge.
- Data fabric (inference runtime workloads) will be in an isolated L2/L3 segment per tenant with strict ACLs and mTLS sidecars between runtime pods and the control-plane proxies.
- Prefix/pod NAT is optional — we included a port-binding catalog (port-binding-catalog.xlsx) because Stellar asked for predictable source ports for their SIEM.

Questions for Rackline and Stellar:
- Rackline: can you confirm you can provision the VLANs and eBGP sessions as drawn? Any constraints on BGP communities or route-filtering we should be aware of?
- Stellar: do you have any upstream requirements for outbound IP stability or egress logging (we included a runbook section for optional egress pools)?

Proposed follow-ups: light architecture review tomorrow 11/23 9:30am PST — I can send a calendar invite after we confirm.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
(attachment: mgmt-data-fabric-v1.png, runbook-draft-tenant-segmentation.pdf, port-binding-catalog.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Mgmt + Data Fabric: private VPC attachment and reference diagram review

Thanks Soojin — quick set of comments after skimming the diagram:

1) Control plane HA: I agree with colocating control-plane masters in the management fabric, but we should explicitly call out a second availability zone peer (AZ-B) for etcd quorum. If this deployment is single-colo, we should use a 3-node etcd spread across two racks + a witness VM to avoid split-brain risk.

2) BGP / adjacency: prefer eBGP between management fabric leafs and Rackline's edge routers. For tenant data-plane we should avoid injecting tenant prefixes directly to Stellar’s global table — instead we advertise only the egress/ingress NAT prefixes and keep tenant-local CIDRs internal to the colo.

3) KV/Cache path isolation: add a small note about separate east-west QoS for KV cache (gRPC) traffic so inference tail latency isn't impacted by bulk egress backups.

4) Observability: add a dedicated telemetry exporter hop in the management fabric (we can scrape exporter -> central collector) to avoid telemetry spikewash on the runtime nodes.

I'll add a marked-up PNG with annotations and upload to the Drive link by EOD.

-Jonas
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: jonas-annotations-mgmt-data-fabric-v1.png)

From: Rackline Solutions <networking@rackline.co>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@stellar-analytics.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22 19:05 PST
Subject: Re: Mgmt + Data Fabric: private VPC attachment and reference diagram review

Hi Soojin / team — Rackline here. Quick constraints and confirmations from our side: 

- VLANs: we can provision the requested /26 management VLAN and two /24 data VLANs (staging + prod). We will tag per-rack and provide the trunk details.
- BGP: we can run eBGP sessions; however, Stellar's edge requires MD5 on the session and there's a community tagging policy that strips 32-bit ASN communities. Please confirm whether those communities are required for your internal routing policies.
- NAT/egress: we advise using a small pool of stable NAT IPs for production egress (as you suggested). If Stellar requires per-tenant stable IPs, we'll need to reserve a /29 per tenant (lead time: 7 business days).
- Firewall: we can apply stateful ACLs at the leaf, but deep packet inspection (DPI) is a separate managed service — if Stellar needs DPI for egress, we need to add an NDA addendum.

We have uploaded our provisioning checklist to the shared Drive and will stand up the initial VLANs once we have a signed network change window.

— Rackline NetOps
(attachment: rackline-provisioning-checklist.pdf)

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: networking@rackline.co, eng@stellar-analytics.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-23 08:44 PST
Subject: Re: Mgmt + Data Fabric: private VPC attachment and reference diagram review

Thanks Rackline — this is helpful. Short responses and decisions: 

- Jonas: please add the 3-node etcd note and the telemetry exporter hop to the diagram. Also add a short blurb in the runbook about witness VM recovery steps (we'll keep the runbook lightweight).
- Rackline: MD5 auth is fine and communities are not required for the initial rollout — we'll avoid relying on 32-bit community tagging. For production egress, Stellar confirms they want a stable /29 per tenant. Rackline, please raise a reservation ticket and include the lead time in your provisioning checklist.
- Stellar (cc): please confirm whether you want DPI for outbound traffic (this affects timeline and potential NDA). Also confirm the preferred cutover window (we proposed 12/6–12/8 in the doc).

Next steps: Jonas to upload annotated diagram + updated runbook by EOD 11/23. Rackline to provision trunk VLANs in staging and create reservation ticket for /29s. I'll send a calendar invite for a technical walk-through 11/24 9:30am PST once I see the updated artifacts.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
